summary_html: CPS **screens out** a report (no investigation) or closes as **unfounded** after minimal review. Federal law (CAPTA) conditions funding on operating screening criteria and recordkeeping; federal reviews (CFSR) assess decision quality.
authority_html:

- **CFSR Regulations (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal performance/quality review of state screening and responses

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Kyle K. v. Department of Children and Families
key_cases.holding: The Appeals Court upheld a DCF hearing officer's decision affirming a "supported" finding of sexual abuse, holding that judicial review under G. L. c. 30A asks only whether substantial evidence supports the conclusion that there was reasonable cause to believe the abuse occurred, with particular deference to the hearing officer's credibility determinations.
key_cases.relevance: The hearing officer reversed the physical abuse allegation while sustaining the sexual abuse allegation, illustrating allegation-by-allegation unfounding.
key_cases.quote: As to facts, where there is substantial evidence to support the findings of the agency, the court will not substitute its own view of the facts.

key_cases.case_name: Lindsay v. Department of Social Services
key_cases.holding: The SJC clarified that on judicial review of a "supported" finding of abuse or neglect, the court asks only whether substantial evidence supports the hearing officer's conclusion that there was reasonable cause to believe the maltreatment occurred, and it upheld the supported finding of neglect.
key_cases.relevance: Lindsay identifies what an agency must have before it may support rather than screen out or unfound an allegation.
key_cases.quote: there need only be “substantial evidence” supporting the conclusion that there was “reasonable cause to believe” that Lindsay neglected Adrianna

key_cases.holding: The Appeals Court affirmed termination, holding that homelessness, poverty and financial instability cannot alone support termination but may properly be considered as part of the unfitness determination where they are tied to the parent's inability to provide minimally adequate care.
key_cases.relevance: Virgil marks the line between conditions of poverty, which do not by themselves justify intervention, and parenting deficits that do.
key_cases.quote: While homelessness, poverty, and financial instability alone are not sufficient to terminate a person's parental rights, they are proper considerations in an unfitness determination.

key_cases.case_name: Covell v. Department of Social Services
key_cases.holding: The SJC affirmed the department's decision to "support" an allegation of sexual abuse and to list the plaintiff in its registry of alleged perpetrators, holding that a supported finding requires only reasonable cause to believe the abuse occurred, that the substantial evidence test does not become more stringent because the consequences of the agency decision are severe, and that hearsay bearing indicia of reliability can by itself be substantial evidence.
key_cases.relevance: Covell fixes what the department must have before it may support rather than unsupport an allegation: reasonable cause to believe, not proof that the abuse in fact occurred.
key_cases.quote: Substantial evidence may be based on hearsay alone if that hearsay has "indicia of reliability."

timeline_requirements.deadline: 24 hours for the interim report and initial determination on the child's safety and custody (emergency response)

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: No penalty stated in M.G.L. c. 119, § 51B(c)

timeline_requirements.deadline: 5 business days (emergency response) or 15 business days (non-emergency response) for the written determination whether the abuse or neglect is substantiated
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Initial contact on a screened-in 51A report
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: No penalty stated in M.G.L. c. 119, § 51B; the 15-business-day determination may be extended only by a waiver approved by the DCF area director or requested by law enforcement (§ 51B(d))
